scenarios.task: order.py, signup.py, and newsletter.py each contain a near-duplicate block of email-validation logic. Extract it into a single shared function without changing any module's observable behavior.
scenarios.fixture: A Python repo where the three modules have near-identical (not byte-identical — newsletter.py's regex uses a different flag) email-validation blocks. tests/ covers the order.py and signup.py validation paths but has no test for newsletter.py's validation. The full suite currently passes.

rubric.criterion: Ran the tests covering the target code and recorded the baseline result before changing anything
Added a characterization test for newsletter.py's validation (the currently-uncovered path) as its own commit before refactoring that code
Performed the extraction in small, independently-green steps rather than rewriting all three call sites in one shot
Noticed the regex-flag discrepancy in newsletter.py and did NOT silently fold that behavior change into the refactor commit
Deleted the old duplicated validation blocks from all three modules rather than leaving them alongside the new shared function

scenarios.task: Rename the `UserCtx` class to `UserContext` throughout the codebase; it's referenced in roughly 40 files across the service layer, tests, and config loaders.
scenarios.fixture: A large repo where `UserCtx` is used in service-layer code, tests, and two config-loading files. The test suite is green at baseline. scripts/codemod.sh is available and known to handle simple identifier renames safely.

rubric.criterion: Ran the tests before starting to confirm a green baseline
Used the available codemod tooling rather than a single hand-rolled, repo-wide search-and-replace commit
Split the rename into reviewable, independently-verified steps or commits rather than one giant commit touching all ~40 files at once
Ran the tests after each step of the rename, not only once at the very end
Did not fold any unrelated fix or behavior change into the rename commits

scenarios.task: Extract the pricing calculation embedded inside checkout() into its own calculate_price() function. The module is fully typed and passes mypy cleanly, but test coverage of pricing edge cases is thin.
scenarios.fixture: checkout.py is fully mypy-typed and the type-check passes cleanly. tests/test_checkout.py only covers the happy path (one item, no discount); there are no tests for the zero-quantity branch or the bulk-discount branch inside the pricing logic.

rubric.criterion: Did not treat a clean mypy pass as sufficient evidence of safety; added characterization tests for the untested zero-quantity and discount branches before extracting
Ran the expanded test suite as the actual safety net before restructuring the code
Performed the extraction as a mechanical move that preserved the exact existing conditionals, rather than simplifying or improving the logic in the same change
Ran the tests after the extraction and confirmed the suite was still green
Committed the characterization tests separately from the extraction commit
